source: Recorded with tee-cli.ts in front of Claude Code 2.1.322 through ADE CORE's ClaudeBackend in supervised mode: a ScheduleWakeup of 60 s and the turn it woke, then CronCreate for a one-shot and a recurring job, three turns they fired, and CronDelete. A woken or fired turn has no user frame and a `result` without `origin`. `stopHookInputs` holds what a Stop command hook in the throwaway project received after each turn: `session_crons` lists each job as `{ id, schedule, recurring, prompt }`, with a pending wakeup among them as a one-shot, and no next run time. Stream events, rate limits, control traffic, hooks and init are left out.

content.text: Call the ScheduleWakeup tool once with delaySeconds 60, reason "capture", and prompt "Reply with the single word woken." Then end your turn with the word scheduled.

input.prompt: Reply with the single word woken.

content.content: Next wakeup scheduled for 10:31:00 (in 79s). If you owe the user a status update this tick, write it now as ordinary response text; then end the turn — the harness re-invokes you when the wakeup fires or a task-notification arrives.

content.text: Use CronCreate twice. First a one-shot job that fires once, about one minute from now, with the prompt "Reply with the single word once." Then a recurring job every minute with the prompt "Reply with the single word repeat." Then end your turn with the word created.
